You're working on Nxeon, a hosting platform (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). `/opt/nxeon` is production (git, origin/main). `/opt/nxeon-staging` is a separate staging checkout with its own DB, used for verification before anything touches prod. Read `/root/.claude/... ` — no, disregard that, just use what's below; you have no access to prior session memory, everything you need is here.

## The task — two parts, both real product changes

The owner wants the Domains page (`app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx`) redesigned to match a reference screenshot (a Hostinger-style layout — Nxeon is explicitly a Hostinger-style host, so matching that product-category convention is intentional, not copying a competitor's brand). They ALSO want a genuinely new feature: every domain registration includes a real, working free-tier email inbox, with the ability to actually set up that mailbox's address DURING the registration flow — not a marketing-only claim.

## Part 1 — Visual redesign of the Domains list page

Current file: `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx` (279 lines) — read it fully first. It currently has: a `PortalHero` header with Transfer/Find-name/Register buttons, a `DomainSearch` component, 3 stat cards (Domains/Active/Expiring soon), then either an `EmptyState` or a responsive card-grid (mobile) / table (desktop) of domains with columns Domain/Status/Expires/DNS/Price/Auto-renew/Actions.

Target reference layout (described from a screenshot the owner shared — recreate the STRUCTURE and INFORMATION DENSITY, not literal pixel values, and use Nxeon's real design tokens/components, not generic ones):
- 4 stat cards instead of 3: Total Domains, Expiring Soon, Expiring Today (NEW — domains expiring today specifically, distinct from "within 30 days"), Auto Renew On (NEW — count of domains with `autoRenew: true`).
- A cross-sell banner: "Every domain comes with a FREE Business Email Inbox" with a short sub-line and a "Learn More" link — see Part 2, this must be a TRUE claim once you build the feature, not just copy.
- A "Find your perfect domain" search card containing: the domain search input (reuse/extend the existing `DomainSearch` component, don't rebuild it from scratch — check what it already does first), a row of quick-pick TLD price pills (.com, .io, .co, .net, .org, .online — pull REAL current prices from wherever `DomainSearch`/the registrar integration already sources TLD pricing, do not hardcode fake prices), and a small promo card (e.g. "Get .COM for $X" using the REAL current .com price, not an invented one).
- Right sidebar (new — the current page is single-column, this needs a two-column layout on larger screens): "Register a new domain" CTA card, "Transfer a domain" CTA card (only if `transfersAvailable()` — mirror the existing conditional), a "Quick Actions" card (Manage DNS, Contact Information, Child Nameservers, Domain Lock — link these to real existing pages/routes if they exist; if a route doesn't exist yet for one of these, either omit it or link to the closest existing equivalent, don't invent a dead link), and a "Need Help?" card with links to real existing help/support pages (check `KB_PAGES` in `lib/kb-system.ts` or the site's actual help-center routes for real URLs — don't invent URLs).
- The domain table gains an "Email Inbox" column showing each domain's mailbox status (Active + mailbox count, or a "Set up" CTA if not yet configured) and a "Nameservers" column. Keep the existing mobile card-grid / desktop table responsive split — extend both, don't drop mobile support.
- Use Nxeon's real design tokens throughout (the `card`, `card glass`, `btn-primary`/`btn-secondary`, `StatCard`, `Badge`, `StatusDot` components already used in the current file — check `components/ui/primitives.tsx` for what's available before inventing new UI primitives). The brand palette is navy+violet+cyan (`brand-*`/`accent-*` CSS variables in `app/globals.css` — grep for the exact token names already in use in this same file and nearby dashboard pages). Do not drift into a generic/templated look — match how OTHER dashboard pages in this app already look (check `app/dashboard/page.tsx` or `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` for the established visual language of stat cards + sidebars if any exist there).

## Part 2 — Real free-tier email inbox with every domain registration

This is a genuine product/pricing decision already made by the owner: **build it for real**, not a marketing-only banner.

1. **Define a free email tier.** Look at `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `EmailPlan` model (`mailboxes`, `storageGB`, `priceCents`, `termMonths`, `active`, `sortOrder`) and the real paid tiers in `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts` (Starter/Business/Pro — check exact current mailbox/storage numbers there, don't guess). Add a new seeded `EmailPlan` row: `priceCents: 0`, a small, genuinely-free-tier-appropriate `mailboxes` (1) and `storageGB` (look at what's realistic given the paid Starter tier's storage — pick something noticeably smaller, e.g. 1-2GB, so it's a real free tier and not identical to a paid one), name it clearly (e.g. "Free" or "Domain Inbox"), and mark it `active: true`. Add this via a migration/seed script consistent with how other `EmailPlan` rows are seeded (check `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts`'s exact pattern and either extend it or add a small idempotent seed script — check if seed scripts in this repo are re-run automatically or need manual execution, and follow the established convention).

2. **Wire it into domain registration.** `lib/actions-domains.ts`'s `purchaseDomain` (read the full function — it validates a domain, debits the wallet, calls the registrar API, and creates the `Domain` record) is the entry point. After a domain registration succeeds, create a real `EmailSubscription` row (same model `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts` uses — read `orderEmailHostingCore` in that file for the exact pattern of creating a subscription + actually provisioning the mailbox on Mailcow via `provisionMailboxOnMailcow`) tied to the new domain, using the new free `EmailPlan`. This needs real DNS (MX records) pointed at Nxeon's mail infrastructure for the new domain — check how `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts` handles DNS for an "in-account" domain (a domain Nxeon manages, which this now IS, since it was just registered through Nxeon) versus an external domain; a domain registered THROUGH Nxeon should get automatic DNS/MX setup with no manual verification step required (mirror whatever code path `orderEmailHosting` uses for its "domain in your account" case).

3. **Let the customer choose the mailbox address during registration**, not have one silently assigned. Find `components/customer/DomainRegisterWizard.tsx` (used by `app/dashboard/domains/register/page.tsx`) and read its full step structure. Add a step (or a section within an existing step, your judgment on the best placement — likely right before or as part of the final review/confirm step) where the customer can:
   - See that a free inbox is included, with its real limits (1 mailbox, X GB — from the plan you created).
   - Enter the mailbox's local-part (e.g. "hello" → `hello@theirdomain.com`) with the same live availability-shaped UI pattern already used in `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx`'s "NEW MAILBOX" input (placeholder "hello", `@domain.com` suffix shown inline, an "Add mailbox" style action) — reuse that established convention rather than inventing new UI for the same concept.
   - Allow skipping — the free inbox should still be reserved/available even if they don't set an address right now (they can add one later from `/dashboard/email` or wherever mailbox management already lives), so don't make this step blocking.
   - Thread the chosen local-part (if provided) through `purchaseDomain`'s form data into the new `EmailSubscription`+mailbox-creation logic from step 2, so the mailbox gets created with the RIGHT address immediately rather than a generic default. If they skip, still create the `EmailSubscription` (so the domain "has" its included free inbox and shows correctly on the redesigned Domains page from Part 1) but don't create an actual mailbox until they add one later.

4. **Existing domains**: do NOT retroactively grant free mailboxes to every domain already registered on the platform — that's a separate, larger cost decision the owner hasn't made. Only new registrations from this change forward get one. Say this explicitly in your report so it's a visible, understood scope boundary, not a silent omission.

5. Update the Domains page's new "Email Inbox" column (Part 1) to reflect this real state per domain: shows the mailbox status/count for domains with a real `EmailSubscription`, and a "Set up" CTA linking to wherever mailbox creation lives for domains registered before this feature shipped (or for anyone who skipped step 3).

## Verification discipline
1. Baseline BEFORE any changes: `cd /opt/nxeon && npm test 2>&1 | grep "^not ok"` (expect 34 pre-existing failures, all pricing/proration/auth-flavored — none about domains/email).
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after all changes.
3. `npm test` failure set identical to baseline after.
4. Commit incrementally (e.g. one commit for the schema+seed, one for the registration backend wiring, one for the wizard UI, one for the page redesign) — each ending in:
   ```

   Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   ```
   `git push origin main` after each — retry once after 2s on "cannot lock ref" (transient, known issue, other work lands on main concurrently from elsewhere in this session, not a real conflict).
5. If you add a new column to `EmailPlan`/`EmailSubscription` or any model — check first whether you actually need a NEW column or whether the existing schema already supports everything (a new EmailPlan row + EmailSubscription row likely needs NO schema changes at all, just new data — prefer that). If you truly need a schema change, this repo uses hand-written SQL files under `prisma/manual-migration-*.sql` applied MANUALLY to production's database (see the existing files there for the format) — schema changes are NOT part of `scripts/promote-production.sh`. Do NOT apply anything to production's database yourself under any circumstances — write the migration SQL file, commit it, and say clearly in your final report that a human needs to review and apply it before this can be promoted. This is a hard rule: a schema change silently applied to a live production database without review already caused real risk earlier today.
6. Deploy to staging: `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (this DOES run `prisma db push` automatically against staging's own separate database — safe there). May background-timeout the calling shell call — check its output file rather than re-running.
7. Verify LIVE on staging with Playwright (`/opt/nxeon-staging/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`, `chromium.launch()` + `newContext({ bypassCSP: true })`, login `claude-audit-2026@nxeon.test` / `AuditPass123!` at `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`): register a real domain end-to-end through the wizard including setting a mailbox address, land on the redesigned Domains page, and confirm via a direct Prisma query against staging's database that a real `EmailSubscription` row and (if you provided an address) a real mailbox record were created — don't just trust the UI, prove the data. Take screenshots of the redesigned page and the wizard's new mailbox step.

## Hard constraints
- Do **NOT** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` — staging only, the owner reviews before promoting.
- Do **NOT** apply any database migration to production yourself, even if it looks tiny/safe — write the SQL file and flag it for review, per the hard rule above.
- Do not run `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon` itself — only `tsc --noEmit`/`npm test` are safe there.
- Don't invent fake pricing, fake URLs, or fake feature claims — every number and link on the redesigned page must trace back to something real in the codebase/database.
- Don't scope-creep beyond what's described. Note anything else you notice in your final report instead of fixing it inline.

## Final report
What you built for the redesign and for the free-inbox feature, the exact free-tier specs you chose and why, whether a manual migration file needs review (if so, its exact contents and why), verification results (tsc/test-diff, staging deploy, the real Prisma-confirmed EmailSubscription/mailbox row, screenshots), and any judgment calls (e.g. exact wording of the banner, where you placed the mailbox-setup step in the wizard, what you did for existing domains).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2

chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true

systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker

echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"

/**
 * Refuse to write to a database nobody deliberately pointed us at.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE INCIDENT THIS EXISTS FOR (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * An agent ran `prisma/seed.ts` from a scratch working tree. That tree had its
 * `node_modules` SYMLINKED to /opt/nxeon/node_modules, so `@prisma/client`
 * resolved through the symlink, and Prisma's dotenv loader walked up from the
 * REAL module location and loaded `/opt/nxeon/.env` — the PRODUCTION env. The
 * seed therefore connected to the production database `nxeon` while every human
 * signal (the cwd, the checkout, the intent) said "scratch".
 *
 * It happened to be a pure `upsert` seed, so it did no damage. That is luck, not
 * a control. The same accident with `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`, or with
 * a seed that had grown a `deleteMany`, destroys a live hosting platform's
 * customer records.
 *
 * The root cause is NOT "the seed was careless". It is that a writing script
 * inherits its target from ambient environment resolution — a mechanism with no
 * confirmation step, which resolves silently and can be wrong for reasons that
 * are invisible at the call site (a symlink three directories away).
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE CONTROL
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * A writing script must state, out loud, which database it believes it is about
 * to write to. The operator states it independently, via `NXEON_DB_TARGET`. The
 * script runs only if the two agree.
 *
 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed.ts
 *
 * This is deliberately NOT a "--force"/"--yes" flag. A blanket confirmation
 * answers "do you want to proceed?", and in the incident above the honest answer
 * was yes — the operator did want to seed, just not THAT database. Naming the
 * target answers the question that was actually wrong. An operator who types
 * `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_scratch` while the environment silently resolves to
 * `nxeon` gets a refusal and a diff, which is exactly the moment the symlink
 * becomes visible.
 *
 * Pure and side-effect free so it can be unit-tested without a database; see
 * test/db-target-guard.test.ts.
 */

/** Environment variable through which the operator names the intended database. */
export const TARGET_ENV_VAR = "NXEON_DB_TARGET";

export type DbTargetDecision =
  | { allowed: true; database: string }
  | { allowed: false; database: string | null; message: string };

/**
 * Extract the database NAME from a PostgreSQL connection URL.
 *
 * Returns null when the URL is absent, unparseable, or names no database. We do
 * not guess: a connection string we cannot read is a connection string we cannot
 * confirm, and the whole point here is to stop acting on unconfirmed targets.
 */
export function databaseNameFromUrl(url: string | undefined | null): string | null {
  if (!url) return null;

All 5 of my commits are on `origin/main`, and the untracked files are pre-existing clutter from other concurrent work in `/opt/nxeon` — none of them are mine, so I left them untouched. This work is complete. Here is the final report.

## What shipped

**Part 1 — Domains list redesign** (`app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainSearch.tsx`)
- 4 stat cards (Total domains, Expiring soon, Expiring today, Auto renew on), a cross-sell banner with real numbers, a two-column layout (`lg:grid-cols-[1fr_340px]`, matching the ratio `DomainRegisterWizard` already uses for its own aside), and a sidebar (Register/Transfer CTAs, Quick Actions scoped to the most-recent domain, Need Help).
- New **Email Inbox** and **Nameservers** columns on both the desktop table and mobile card grid, reflecting real per-domain `EmailSubscription`/`Mailbox` state — never a placeholder.
- `DomainSearch`'s idle-state TLD row was upgraded (not rebuilt) from bare tags into priced pills + a `.com` promo card, sourced from the existing `components/marketing/tlds.ts` `POPULAR_TLDS` catalog (the same "indicative from-price" data already used elsewhere) — no invented numbers.
- Quick Actions omits "Contact Information" entirely (no such feature exists in this codebase — registrant contact isn't even persisted) and relabels "Child Nameservers" to "Nameservers" (the real feature is custom nameservers, not ICANN child/glue records) rather than link to something that doesn't exist.

**Part 2 — Free Domain Inbox** 
- **No schema change** — a free tier only needed a new `EmailPlan` row. Mirrored the codebase's own existing pattern for this exact situation (`prisma/seed-hosting-email-plans.ts` + `lib/hosting-email.ts`): `priceCents: 0, active: false`, name `"Free Domain Inbox"`, `mailboxes: 1, storageGB: 2` (deliberately smaller than paid Starter's 10GB) — `prisma/seed-domain-inbox-plan.ts`, guarded with the `NXEON_DB_TARGET` safety check.
- **Judgment call / deviation from the literal instruction:** the task said to mark the plan `active: true`. I set it `active: false` instead, matching the codebase's established "bundled free plan" convention, because every general-purpose "browse plans" query (`/dashboard/email`, `/dashboard/deploy`, `/pricing`, `/business-email`) filters `active: true` — an `active: true` free plan would have let a customer self-serve it onto an **already-registered** domain through the ordinary Business Email order flow, directly violating the "no retroactive grants" requirement. `active: false` + a dedicated lookup by name closes that loophole while keeping the plan fully real and usable.
- `lib/domain-inbox-email.ts` — a **plain module with no `"use server"` directive** (intentional: exporting the provisioning logic from a Server Actions file would make it a public, directly-callable action with no ownership check, the same class of bug the 2026-07-25 cross-tenant mailbox takeover fix exists to prevent). `purchaseDomain` (`lib/actions-domains.ts`) calls it after a domain registers successfully (both the happy path and the "recovered after registrar error" path): creates a real `EmailSubscription` (`external: false, verified: true` — DNS is already ours, no manual verification step, mirroring `orderEmailHostingCore`'s in-account branch) and, if an address was chosen, a real `Mailbox` + Mailcow provisioning attempt.
- `DomainRegisterWizard` gained a 4th "Email" step (only rendered when the plan is actually seeded — never claims a feature that isn't there), reusing `EmailHosting.tsx`'s local-part + `@domain` suffix convention. Fully skippable — the subscription is still created either way.

**Scope boundary (explicit):** existing domains are **not** retroactively granted a free inbox. Only new registrations from this change forward get one.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npm test` failure set: byte-identical to the 34-failure baseline before any change.
- 5 commits, each pushed to `origin/main` individually (schema+seed → backend wiring → seed-guard fixup → wizard UI → page redesign); two pushes hit the documented transient "cannot lock ref" and succeeded on retry/were already present.
- Deployed to staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh main`), seeded the plan there (`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed-domain-inbox-plan.ts`).
- **Live Playwright run** against `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`, logged in as `claude-audit-2026@nxeon.test`: searched a domain, walked all 5 wizard steps including entering `hello` on the Email step, submitted, landed on the domain detail page, then the redesigned Domains list. **Confirmed directly via Prisma against staging's DB** (not just the UI): `Domain` row ACTIVE, `EmailSubscription` row on the real "Free Domain Inbox" plan (`external:false, verified:true`), `Mailbox` row `hello@<domain>` with `quotaMB: 2048` (2GB), status `PROVISIONING` (expected — Mailcow isn't configured on staging, so it never reaches ACTIVE there, which is the correct failure-tolerant behavior, not a bug).
- Screenshots captured: the wizard's Email step, the Review step showing "Free email inbox: hello@…", and the redesigned Domains list (4 real stats, banner, priced TLD pills, sidebar, Email Inbox/Nameservers columns all showing real "Provisioning" state for the 3 test domains).

## Needs human review before promotion
**No manual migration file was created or is needed** — the entire feature (new plan + subscriptions + mailboxes) uses existing `EmailPlan`/`EmailSubscription`/`Mailbox` columns. Nothing to review on the schema side.

The one manual step for prod: after promotion, someone needs to run `NXEON_DB_TARGET=<prod db name> npx tsx prisma/seed-domain-inbox-plan.ts` once against production (same as any other bundled-plan seed script in this repo) so the "Free Domain Inbox" plan row exists there — the code degrades gracefully if it's missing (Email step just doesn't render), but the feature won't actually work until it's seeded.
